clue.text: The Guardian in trouble, having dismissed a dig's find

indicators.note: letters in trouble are thrown into disorder, so the newspaper's name is to be rearranged
the letters of the following words are sent away from the jumbled pool before it is rearranged

parts.note: the letters A, D, I, G are the ones taken out of the pool

explanation.surface: A newspaper in difficulties has let go of an archaeological excavation's prize discovery.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike A, D, I and G from THE GUARDIAN, leaving T, H, E, U, R, A, N, and rearrange those seven. The 's is 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition 'find'.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth something is to discover or dig it up, a verb synonym of find.

clue.text: Type who exploits trick, right to the end

indicators.note: the letter is shifted from the front of the word to its end

parts.note: a ruse is a trick

explanation.surface: Describes a manipulator who plays dirty tricks right up to the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is a person who takes advantage of others for their own ends.

clue.text: Occasionally perplexed seeing weapon

indicators.note: taking only some letters at regular gaps, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: Someone is now and then baffled at the sight of a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: An épée is a fencing sword with a stiff blade.

clue.text: Uniform maybe used once marine's served time

indicators.note: serving a dish can mean dishing it out mixed up, so the letters of marine are rearranged

parts.note: the word marine; the 's is 'has'

explanation.surface: A marine who has done his tour of duty, and the uniform he once wore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served time' looks like a jail term, but 'served' is the anagram signal and T stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an archaic word for clothing, which is why the clue says 'used once' of a uniform as an example.

clue.text: Greg the Trade Minister accepting electronic bus is economically efficient

indicators.note: the surname takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: Greg Hands was a UK government minister for trade
USB stands for Universal Serial Bus, an electronic connection standard

explanation.surface: A trade minister endorsing electric buses as a thrifty choice.
explanation.walkthrough: Greg Hands is a British Conservative MP who served as a trade minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who husbands resources manages them frugally and carefully, the verb form of thrift.

clue.text: His Majesty rejected "hot-desking" out of hand, and took the chair

indicators.note: something out of hand is out of control, so the letters of hot-desking are to be jumbled
the monarch's letters are thrown out of the pool before it is rearranged

parts.note: a male sovereign addressed as His Majesty is a king

explanation.surface: The monarch dismissed the office practice of hot-desking outright and presided over the meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Take KING out of HOTDESKING to leave HOTDES, then rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hosted a meeting presided over it, just as a chairperson does.

clue.text: Ham and eggs eaten up by the mouth

indicators.note: spoken by the mouth, so the words are taken as they sound

parts.note: eggs are ova, and eaten up (with worry) is racked; said together the two words make the sound

explanation.surface: A breakfast plate of ham and eggs devoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham and eggs' looks like a breakfast, but 'Ham' is the definition. Said aloud, OVA RACKED sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform in an exaggerated, theatrical manner.

clue.text: Irksome work at home uncovered better material

parts.note: toil is hard, wearisome work
in means at home

indicators.note: the outer letters, the cover, are removed from better

explanation.surface: Tedious domestic chores gave way to a superior fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilinette is a woollen fabric once used for waistcoats.

clue.text: Exhausted following gender reassignment police officer initially belittled

indicators.note: the officer's letters are placed at the start

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: the letter for female is reassigned to the letter for male

parts.note: finished can mean exhausted or worn out

explanation.surface: A worn-out officer, demeaned after transitioning.
explanation.walkthrough: F and M are the standard abbreviations for female and male, so a gender reassignment swaps one letter for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Diminished means made smaller or less important, i.e. lessened or demeaned.

clue.text: Cowboy's item perhaps ultimately in decline

parts.note: a spur is worn on a cowboy's boot

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of in

explanation.surface: A cowboy's spur might end up going out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: To spurn is to reject or turn down, the verb sense of decline.

clue.text: Rivals see me in fights

indicators.note: letters that fight scuffle and tumble about, so see me in is to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A boxer taunts opponents, telling them they'll meet him in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Enemies are opponents or adversaries, the same idea as rivals.

clue.text: Eli's back in before mother superior

parts.note: pre is the Latin-derived prefix meaning before

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the word for mother

parts.note: mum is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: the back of Eli is its final letter

parts.note: Eli is a man's name; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A man named Eli has returned to the convent ahead of the Mother Superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother superior' reads as a nun's title, but 'mother' is wordplay and 'superior' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Premium as an adjective means of high quality, top-grade, which is what superior means.

clue.text: Extradition possibly helping to secure nasty pirate

indicators.note: the outer word holds the other one fast inside it

parts.note: a ration is a portion or helping of food

indicators.note: something turned nasty is twisted out of shape, so pirate is rearranged

explanation.surface: Sending a vicious buccaneer back for trial, with an assistant helping to hold him.
explanation.definitionFit: Extradition is one example of sending a person back to their own country, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Rest area and place for service wagon to back up

parts.note: a church is where a religious service is held

indicators.note: backing up in a down clue means reading the word upward, i.e. reversed

parts.note: a dray is a low cart or wagon, as used by brewers

explanation.surface: A lay-by and a service station where a lorry can reverse in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest area' and 'service' suggest a motorway stop, but the rest here is eternal.
explanation.definitionFit: A churchyard is a burial ground, where the dead are laid to rest.

clue.text: Opening of an American court case overlooking one Scotsman in Dundee, perhaps

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: US is short for United States, i.e. American

indicators.note: overlooking means missing out, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: a trial is a case heard in court
I is the Roman numeral one
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: An American court case begins, ignoring a Scot from the city of Dundee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotsman in Dundee' suggests Scotland, but Dundee is Mick 'Crocodile' Dundee, the film's Australian hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocodile Dundee is the title character of an Australian film, an example of a man from Australia.

clue.text: TV show about fugitives keeping adult obsessed

indicators.note: the show's title keeps the letter held inside it

parts.note: Hunted is a British reality television series in which contestants try to evade capture as fugitives
A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A television programme about people on the run that has grown-ups glued to the screen.
explanation.walkthrough: Hunted is a UK reality show where ordinary people go on the run from a team of trackers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone haunted by an idea is preoccupied with it and cannot let it go.

clue.text: Head off troubles and rest

indicators.note: the head of the word, its first letter, is cut off

parts.note: bothers means troubles or worries

explanation.surface: Advice to stave off worries and take a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' looks like a verb meaning prevent, but it tells you to drop the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The others are the remaining ones, i.e. the rest of a group.

clue.text: One type of music, southern soul

parts.note: in ancient Egyptian belief the ka is the spiritual double or soul

explanation.surface: A description of a musical genre as being from the American South and full of soul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Southern soul' looks like a music genre, but it is two separate pieces of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ska is a Jamaican genre of popular music, a forerunner of reggae.

clue.text: Supposedly Arsenal's No.1 fumbled shot — that's awful

indicators.note: number one indicates the first letter
a fumbled shot is botched, so its letters are mixed up

parts.note: ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: An Arsenal striker supposedly scuffed his shot, and the fans groaned.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: As though means as if, introducing something only supposed or apparent.

clue.text: Unusually stocky pugilist's last to appear in spell of boxing

indicators.note: the letter appears inside the word for a boxing period

parts.note: a round is one period of a boxing bout

indicators.note: the last letter of pugilist is taken

parts.note: a pugilist is a boxer; the 's is possessive

explanation.surface: A tubby prizefighter finally shows up for a round in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotund describes a plump, rounded figure, noticeably stout in build.

clue.text: Such is no rambling letter (for the most part)

definitions.text: Such is no rambling letter (for the most part)

indicators.note: rambling text wanders about, so the letters are rearranged
only most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A short note card is never a long, wandering missive.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a small sheet for brief messages is not one for rambling letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded card for writing a short message.

clue.text: Shroud the woman filled with passion

indicators.note: the pronoun is filled with the other word

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
heat can mean passion or intensity of feeling

explanation.surface: Cover up a woman who is overcome with ardour.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe is to encase or cover something, as a shroud wraps a body.

clue.text: Where A Boost For All is a rule every student forsakes

indicators.note: a boost lifts things up, which in a down clue reverses the letters
the letters are abandoned from the phrase

parts.note: L, for learner, is the abbreviation for student; every one of them is removed

explanation.surface: An EU-style slogan claiming a universal benefit becomes a rule pupils ignore.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove every L from ALL IS A RULE to leave AISARUE, then 'A Boost For' lifts it, giving the reversal in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurasia is the combined landmass of Europe and Asia, a place, so it answers the question 'where'.

clue.text: Origin of brother, first one slain in confounded Tower

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

parts.note: in Genesis, Abel is the first person killed, by his brother Cain

explanation.surface: The Bible's tale of a brother murdered, set within a tower of confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, God confounded the builders' language at the Tower of Babel.

clue.text: Academy bosses possibly bother eminent scientists, penning note

indicators.note: the first word pens, or encloses, the note

parts.note: a headache is a nuisance or bother
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
RS stands for the Royal Society, Britain's academy of eminent scientists

explanation.surface: Head teachers at academies might pester distinguished scientists while writing them a note.
explanation.walkthrough: An academy is a type of state-funded English school, so its bosses could be head teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: Head teachers run schools, and English academies are one such kind of school.

clue.text: Revised half of Chabrier's letters for another composer

indicators.note: revised letters are reworked into a new order
only the first half of the name's eight letters is kept

parts.note: Emmanuel Chabrier was a French composer

explanation.surface: A rewritten section of a Chabrier score turns into a work by a different composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Sebastian Bach was a German Baroque composer.

clue.text: Disturb gaol

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to agitate or disturb

explanation.walkthrough: Gaol is the British spelling of jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for agitating something and a slang noun for prison.

clue.text: Natural hollows in ditch bordering unfortunate area

indicators.note: the outer word borders the others on each side

parts.note: to axe is to ditch or scrap something
ill can mean unlucky, as in ill fortune

explanation.surface: Landscape description: hollows in a trench next to a hapless patch of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditch' looks like a noun for a trench, but it is a verb meaning scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Axillae are armpits, the body's natural hollows beneath the shoulders.

clue.text: Disliked newcomer stumped in superior role

parts.note: U denotes upper-class, superior

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the word for role

parts.note: a part is an actor's role
st is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

explanation.surface: An unpopular new arrival is baffled after landing a senior position.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman stumped is out when the wicketkeeper breaks the wicket while they are out of their ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is a person who has risen suddenly and behaves arrogantly, and is resented for it.

clue.text: They're taboo when safeguarding heart in restaurants?

definitions.text: They're taboo when safeguarding heart in restaurants?

indicators.note: the first word safeguards, or holds inside, the letter

parts.note: don'ts are things you must not do

indicators.note: the heart of restaurants is its central letter

explanation.surface: Sugary fried treats are off the menu for diners protecting their cardiac health.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: anyone looking after their heart should keep away from these when eating out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ring-shaped fried cakes, high in sugar and fat, are just what a heart-healthy diet forbids.

clue.text: Hotel decorated in warmer shade of purple

indicators.note: the outer word is decorated with the letter placed in it

parts.note: a heater is something that warms
Hotel is the radio alphabet's word for H

explanation.surface: A hotel's bedrooms painted in a warmer purple tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Heather is a pale purplish colour named after the flowering moorland shrub.
